title: A positive test, and what it is worth

prereqs.why: The whole calculation is one application of the theorem.
You need to be fluent in which side of the bar each given number sits on.

statement:
A condition affects $1$ person in $200$. A screening test has:

- **sensitivity $0.99$** — $\P(\text{positive} \mid \text{has it}) = 0.99$;
- **specificity $0.95$** — $\P(\text{negative} \mid \text{does not have it}) = 0.95$.

A person is screened at random and tests **positive**.

What is $\P(\text{has it} \mid \text{positive})$? Give the exact probability.
hints: Write down the four numbers you have been given and which conditional each one is. The answer is a different conditional from any of them, which is the point.
Imagine $20\,000$ people. How many have the condition, and of those how many test positive? How many do not have it, and of *those* how many test positive anyway?
Of $20\,000$: $100$ have it, and $99$ of them test positive. $19\,900$ do not, and $5\%$ of them — $995$ — test positive anyway. So $99$ of $99 + 995$ positives are real.

payload.prompt: The probability that a person testing positive really has the condition.
payload.label: Probability
payload.syntax: A fraction or an expression. You can write it as a quotient of the numbers you computed.
